-Give a thread its records out of what was kept aside.
-The first request of a thread allocates the tld of the thread and its theap. Where
-that found no memory the request failed, whether or not it can fail. What the
-embedder and mimalloc keep for a thread is kept in the tld
-remembered either and the embedder could not ask again.
-A thread without them can allocate nothing, so with an embedder that keeps address
-space aside (ask-who-may-take-address-space.patch) they are a request that cannot
-fail: where they find no memory the thread asks for them again as such a request.
-It allocates them from `theap_meta`, and until it has a tld of its own the tld of
-`theap_meta` stands in for it, for one thread at a time.
-A throwing `new` on a thread that still has no tld does not say that it cannot
-fail: the thread may get its tld before the request has ended, and the end would be
-counted in another word than the beginning.
-Without such an embedder a thread runs what it ran before.
